## Overview

ast2ast has no global seed. Random numbers come from engine and distribution
objects that live inside the translated function. The numbers are the same as
those of R after `set.seed(seed)` with the default `RNGkind()`.

| Function | Result | R equivalent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mersenne_twister(seed)` | engine | `set.seed(seed)` |
| `normal(engine, mean = 0, sd = 1)` | distribution | |
| `uniform(engine, min = 0, max = 1)` | distribution | |
| `draw(dist, n)` | double vector of length `n` | `rnorm(n, mean, sd)` / `runif(n, min, max)` |
| `sample(engine, x, size, replace, prob)` | vector, base type of `x` | `sample(...)` |
| `sample_int(engine, n, size, replace, prob)` | integer vector | `sample.int(...)` |
| `dnorm(x, mean, sd, log)` | density | `dnorm(...)` |
| `dunif(x, min, max, log)` | density | `dunif(...)` |

## Drawing numbers

```{r}
f <- function(seed) {
  argtypes(seed |> type(int))
  e <- mersenne_twister(seed)
  d <- normal(e, mean = 2, sd = 0.5)
  draw(d, 5L)
}
fcpp <- ast2ast::translate(f)
fcpp(1L)

set.seed(1)
rnorm(5, 2, 0.5) # identical
```

Every `draw()` advances the engine of the distribution, so two calls give
different numbers, exactly as two calls of `rnorm`.

`mean`, `sd`, `min`, `max` and `seed` can be read with `$`
(`d$mean`, `e$seed`) but not written.

## Sampling

`sample` and `sample_int` take the engine as first argument. All three
variants of R are supported: without replacement, with replacement and with
`prob`.

```{r}
f <- function(x, p) {
  argtypes(x |> type(vec(double)), p |> type(vec(double)))
  e <- mersenne_twister(6L)
  sample(e, x, 10L, TRUE, p)
}
x <- c(1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5)
p <- c(1, 1, 2, 2, 1)
ast2ast::translate(f)(x, p)

set.seed(6)
sample(x, 10, TRUE, p) # identical
```

As in R, a single number `x >= 1` means `sample(1:x)`.

## Densities

`dnorm` and `dunif` are recycled as in R; the result is a scalar if `x` and
the parameters are scalars. They work in every translation; `dnorm` has
derivatives w.r.t. `x`, `mean` and `sd`, `dunif` w.r.t. `min` and `max`.
This makes them usable in log-likelihoods for `lbfgsb`, `hessian` or HMC.

```{r}
nll <- function(theta, y) {
  argtypes(theta |> type(vec(double)), y |> type(vec(double)))
  -sum(dnorm(y, theta[[1L]], exp(theta[[2L]]), log = TRUE))
}
fcpp <- ast2ast::translate(nll, derivative = "reverse")

set.seed(1)
y <- rnorm(50, mean = 3, sd = 2)
theta <- c(3, log(2))
fcpp(theta, y)
-sum(dnorm(y, 3, 2, log = TRUE)) # same value
```

## Each distribution owns its engine

`normal(e)` and `uniform(e)` store a **copy** of `e`. Consequences:

- Two distributions created from the same engine produce the same stream.

  ```{r}
  f <- function() {
    e <- mersenne_twister(3L)
    a <- normal(e)
    b <- normal(e)
    c(draw(a, 3L), draw(b, 3L)) # rep(rnorm(3), 2) after set.seed(3)
  }
  ```

  Use different seeds for independent streams.
- Drawing from `a` does not advance `e`, and `sample(e, ...)` does not
  advance `a`.
- Mixing distributions is therefore not identical to R. In R,
  `rnorm(2); runif(2)` share one stream; in ast2ast each distribution has its
  own.

## Passing to inner functions

Pass engines and distributions with `ref()`. Passed by value, the inner
function draws from a copy, and the caller later draws the same numbers again.
ast2ast warns at translation time in this case.

```{r}
f <- function() {
  g <- function(d) {
    argtypes(d |> type(normal) |> ref())
    returntype(vec(double))
    draw(d, 2L)
  }
  d <- normal(mersenne_twister(9L))
  c(g(d), g(d)) # rnorm(4) after set.seed(9)
}
```

A `const()` parameter is an error, since drawing changes the object.

## Order of evaluation

C++ does not specify the order in which function arguments are evaluated
(GCC evaluates right to left); R evaluates left to right. With several draws
in one expression the result can therefore differ from R:

```{r}
f <- function() {
  d <- normal(mersenne_twister(1L))
  c(draw(d, 2L), draw(d, 2L)) # the two halves may be swapped
}
```

Assign each draw to a variable first:

```{r}
f <- function() {
  d <- normal(mersenne_twister(1L))
  a <- draw(d, 2L)
  b <- draw(d, 2L)
  c(a, b) # rnorm(4) after set.seed(1)
}
```

## Limitations

- Engines and distributions cannot be passed from R or returned to R.
- The type names `mersenne_twister`, `normal` and `uniform` are reserved;
  `new_type()` cannot reuse them.
- Only the Mersenne-Twister engine and the normal and uniform distribution
  are available. No `p*`/`q*` functions yet.
- `sample` without replacement and without `prob` differs from R for
  `x > 1e7` and `size <= x / 2` (R then uses hashing).
